title: Mining Software Repair Models for Reasoning on the Search Space of Automated Program Fixing
review_status: full-text audit complete; repair-action dataset, model assumptions, modeled search effort, and validity boundaries reviewed
sections_checked: §II AST change corpus and project counts
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2013-11-14; exact v1 PDF audited; Empirical Software Engineering 2013 version identified in PDF
evidence_note: Analyzes 89,993 transactions from 14 Java repositories (62,179 with Java changes) and models attempts over 23,048 small fix transactions. Attempt counts are a probabilistic search-space analysis, not measured end-to-end runtime; authors disclaim precision/recall as the classifier objective and warn about sampling/language limits.

title: Alternation in Quantum Programming: From Superposition of Data to Superposition of Programs
review_status: full-text audit complete; quantum-language semantics and illustrative examples reviewed; not an APR outcome study
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2014-02-20; exact v1 HTML audited
evidence_note: Defines quantum alternation/choice and formal semantics with illustrative examples. It reports no repair success, implementation benchmark, or comparative verification workload; retained as a broad PL/formal-methods item but excluded from APR outcome synthesis.

title: Using Formal Specifications to Support Model Based Testing ASDSpec: A Tool Combining the Best of Two Techniques
review_status: full-text audit complete; ASDSpec container-terminal case study and test-generation/cost caveats reviewed
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2014-03-28; exact v1 PDF audited; EPTCS 141 paper 1 (2014)
evidence_note: ASDSpec creates 93 tests versus 89 from a manually constructed Spec Explorer model in one case study. The 28-hour and 16-hour effort figures are not directly comparable because prior work was reused; generated tests lack system-specific properties.

title: Proceedings 4th International Workshop on Engineering Safety and Security Systems
review_status: sampled arXiv record classified as an edited proceedings volume; official 99-page volume acquired; cover, preface, and contents inspected; constituent papers not individually audited
sections_checked: table of contents and constituent-paper titles
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2015-06-10; EPTCS 184 (2015); exact volume available from official EPTCS mirror
evidence_note: This is not a standalone study: it is a proceedings record for a 99-page volume containing six selected papers from 15 submissions. The volume PDF was inspected at front matter/contents level only; no component paper is counted as full-text audited. Treat as a corpus data-unit anomaly, not substantive repair evidence.

title: Scheduling Constraint Based Abstraction Refinement for Multi-Threaded Program Verification
review_status: full-text audit complete; soundness scope, SV-COMP results, comparison setup, and threats reviewed
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2018-04-03; exact v2 HTML audited
evidence_note: On 1,047 concurrency benchmarks, Yogar-CBMC reports 1,293 points, 1,550 seconds, and 43 GB versus Lazy-CSeq-Abs 9,820 seconds and 104 GB. Guarantees are relative to bounded unwinding; authors flag benchmark and parameter/tool comparison limitations.

title: Low Cost High Integrity Platform
review_status: full-text audit complete; platform architecture, cited deployments, assurance process, and evidence type reviewed
sections_checked: diverse binary generation and runtime checks
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2020-05-14; exact v1 HTML audited
evidence_note: Describes proved B models, dual generated binaries and runtime comparison on separate microcontrollers; cited railway deployments concern platform building blocks. The paper does not provide a controlled cost/defect/certification comparison for this generic-platform report.

title: A Deductive Verification Framework For Higher Order Programs
review_status: full-text audit complete; OCaml/GOSPEL defunctionalization prototype and small case studies reviewed
sections_checked: case studies and automatically discharged conditions
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2020-11-27; exact v1 HTML audited
evidence_note: Prototype translates effectful higher-order OCaml to first-order WhyML and automatically proves conditions on small examples. No large-scale benchmark, success rate, or annotation-effort comparison is reported.

title: MUFIN: Improving Neural Repair Models with Back-Translation
review_status: full-text audit complete; matched-baseline results, oracle localization, correctness labels, and single-hunk boundary reviewed
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2023-04-05; exact v1 PDF audited
evidence_note: MUFIN reports 28 correct/62 plausible Defects4J repairs versus matched baseline 16/43, and 6/7 versus 2/4 on QuixBugs. The experiment assumes perfect localization and uses single-hunk Java bugs; plausible means tests pass, correct means manually judged developer-patch equivalence.

title: Ownership Refinement Types for Pointer Arithmetic and Nested Arrays
review_status: full-text audit complete; soundness theorem, nested-array benchmarks, matched comparison, and annotation/runtime limits reviewed
sections_checked: comparison with prior verifier and Z3-version sensitivity
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2026-04-24; exact v1 HTML audited; ECOOP 2026 version metadata stated in manuscript
evidence_note: Proves soundness for the stated type system and verifies a designed suite of nested-array programs in seconds to about six minutes. Requires richer annotations; benchmark coverage is finite and measured runtime varies with solver version/workload.

title: Agentic Proving for Program Verification
review_status: full-text audit complete; staged Lean results, benchmark defects, conditional headline, and specification-intent limits reviewed
venue_year_verified: arXiv v1 dated 2026-05-22; exact v1 HTML audited
evidence_note: On 161 CLEVER tasks, 95.7% have at least one end-to-end success over two prompt runs; 98.1% is after removing four benchmark-issue entries. The paper flags ground-truth issues in 80/161 tasks and ambiguity between natural-language intent and formal specs, so compile/proof success alone does not establish intent correctness.
